text: The sky above Lara was a bruised purple, bleeding into the orange of the setting sun, but down in the shadows of the pine trees, a single crow perched on a jagged rock. Its feathers were not merely black; they were a deep, iridescent void, shimmering with hints of oil-slick blue and green when the last rays of light caught them. It tilted its head, one bead-black eye fixing on the exhausted climber, a silent witness to her triumph. The bird’s plumage was the color of midnight, of obsidian, of the deepest ink—pure, unadulterated black.
